providers.name: 14th Street Y
providers.shortDescription: 14th Street Y is a lively community center located in the East Village, providing a variety of fitness classes including Yoga, Barre, Pilates, and Zumba. Additionally, it hosts arts and culture events for all ages. The center also offers an infant and toddler center, preschool, after-school programs, and Jewish life events.
providers.longDescription: 14th Street Y is a vibrant community center located in the East Village, welcoming individuals of all ages. It offers a diverse range of classes and activities, including yoga, barre, pilates, and Zumba for fitness enthusiasts, as well as workshops and events for those interested in the arts and culture scene. The center features a dedicated infant and toddler area, providing a nurturing environment for young children. Preschool programs are tailored for kids aged 2 to 5, ensuring a stimulating and engaging experience. For older children, after-school activities keep them active and involved throughout the day. Additionally, the center celebrates Jewish life through various community events. Parents and children can participate in classes together or engage in separate activities that align with their interests, fostering a strong sense of community.

providers.name: 92NY Camp Yomi (2026)
providers.shortDescription: Camp Yomi is 92NY's traditional day-camp track for kindergarten through fourth grade, run on a 50-acre Rockland County campground with bus service from Manhattan.
providers.longDescription: 92NY has run summer camps for more than sixty years, and Camp Yomi is its traditional day-camp track within that history -- a 50-acre Rockland County campground about twenty minutes outside the city, reached by air-conditioned coach buses with onboard bathrooms rather than a standard yellow-bus commute. The day itself is built around two full swims, split between instructional time and free swim, alongside sports like gymnastics and baseball and creative arts including ceramics and jewelry-making. Low staff-to-camper ratios and values-based programming run through the whole day, consistent with 92NY's broader institutional identity rather than a generic camp vendor's approach. For a Manhattan family, the appeal is as much about the bus as the campground itself -- a full Rockland day camp experience without the daily drive.

announcement.title: Bus service from Manhattan
announcement.description: 92NY's camp pages describe coach-bus pickups in Manhattan for the Rockland campground -- see 92NY's own bus map and registration portal for current details.

providers.name: Achilles Kids — Central Park
providers.address: Central Park, Engineer's Gate, New York, NY
providers.shortDescription: Free adaptive running and walking workouts are available at Central Park's Engineer's Gate for children and young adults with disabilities.
providers.longDescription: Achilles Kids is an adaptive athletics program for children and young adults with disabilities, aged 3 to 21. The Manhattan chapter meets at Central Park's Engineer's Gate for in-person running and walking workouts led by trained volunteer guides. Sessions are open to children of all fitness and ability levels, including those with cerebral palsy, spinal cord injuries, traumatic brain injuries, blindness or low vision, cognitive, developmental, and intellectual disabilities, limb difference, and muscular dystrophy. Participants can also join local races with their guides, enhancing fitness, confidence, and community with other Achilles families.

providers.name: Achilles Kids — Prospect Park
providers.address: Prospect Park, Center Drive and Prospect Park East, Brooklyn, NY
providers.shortDescription: Free adaptive running and walking workouts are available in Prospect Park for children and young adults with disabilities.
providers.longDescription: Achilles Kids is an adaptive athletics program for children and young adults with disabilities, aged 3 to 21. The Brooklyn chapter meets at Prospect Park, located at Center Drive and Prospect Park East, for in-person running and walking workouts. These sessions are led by trained volunteer guides and are open to children of all fitness and ability levels. Participants include those with cerebral palsy, spinal cord injuries, traumatic brain injuries, blindness or low vision, cognitive, developmental, and intellectual disabilities, limb difference, and muscular dystrophy. Additionally, participants have the opportunity to join local races with their guides, which helps build fitness, confidence, and a sense of community with other Achilles families.

providers.name: Active Studios NYC
providers.shortDescription: Active Studios NYC provides a range of classes for children, adults, and seniors located on the Upper East Side. These classes cover various activities, including movement, martial arts, dance, and fitness, catering to diverse interests and age groups.
providers.longDescription: Active Studios NYC is a neighborhood studio that provides a range of classes suitable for children, adults, and older adults. The studio focuses on building confidence, connection, and overall well-being through various activities like movement, martial arts, dance, and fitness. Classes are designed to accommodate beginners and are led by expert instructors who create a welcoming environment for all participants.

providers.name: Ahn's Taekwondo NYC
providers.shortDescription: Taekwondo classes are available for children of all ages in a welcoming and family-friendly setting.
providers.longDescription: Ahn's Taekwondo NYC, situated in the heart of the East Village at 20 Avenue A, offers a dynamic and inclusive martial arts experience for students of all ages. The school is led by Grandmaster Anna Y.S. Ahn, who brings decades of expertise to guide learners through their journey. Classes are structured into age-appropriate segments: a lively 30-minute Preschool Martial Arts class designed to introduce the youngest students to basic techniques and discipline; a robust 50-minute Kids Martial Arts class that prepares children for local and national tournaments; and a more advanced 50-minute Teens Martial Arts class tailored for older students. Beyond regular classes, Ahn's Taekwondo NYC provides a supervised After School Program with pickup services for the East Village and Lower East Side, ensuring safety and support during school hours. Weekly Summer Camp sessions focus on screen-free activities, fostering creativity and physical fitness in a fun environment. Birthday parties are also offered, themed around Taekwondo to celebrate young martial artists' special days. New students can experience the community firsthand by signing up for a free trial class.

trial.text: Back to School Special for new members: a free Taekwondo trial class plus a free uniform with new membership enrollment.

providers.name: Aikido of Park Slope
providers.shortDescription: Aikido of Park Slope, Brooklyn's oldest and largest Aikido dojo, teaches self-defense and mindfulness to adults and children under 7th Dan instructor Hal Lehrman.
providers.longDescription: Aikido of Park Slope carries real weight in its own corner of the martial arts world: it describes itself as Brooklyn's oldest and largest Aikido dojo, led by Hal Lehrman, a 7th Dan Aikikai Shihan -- a senior rank most neighborhood dojos simply don't have on staff. The program is deliberately non-competitive, built around self-defense skill, physical fitness and mindfulness rather than tournament results, which tends to suit families looking for a martial art that builds calm and discipline over aggression. Adults and children train at the same dojo, which gives a parent the option to start their own practice alongside a child's rather than just dropping them off elsewhere. A free trial class is the way in, with no cost or commitment required to see whether the dojo's particular style of teaching is the right fit before enrolling in anything.

announcement.title: Led by a 7th Dan Shihan
announcement.description: Brooklyn's oldest and largest Aikido dojo, taught by Hal Lehrman, 7th Dan Aikikai.

trial.text: Book a Free Trial Class

providers.name: All Sports for All People
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn offers a youth sports program that provides swim classes for children as young as 6 months. These classes are held at two Brooklyn high school pools and include baby-and-me lessons and youth swim teams.
providers.longDescription:
All Sports for All People of Camp Olympia offers a comprehensive sports program in Brooklyn designed to help children develop their potential in a supportive and non-punitive atmosphere. The program focuses on teamwork, leadership, and sportsmanship, with dedicated staff guiding each child.

The swimming program caters to a wide range of ages, starting with baby and me classes for infants as young as 6 months. It also includes swim teams and a junior swim team for older children. A swim assessment is available to ensure that new swimmers are placed in the appropriate class. Classes are held at two Brooklyn high school pools: International HS at Prospect Heights and John Jay High School. Families with their own pool can also arrange private lessons with one of the instructors. Additionally, the program offers family swim bundles and gift cards for its classes.

providers.name: April's Dancing Feet
providers.shortDescription: April's Dancing Feet offers a variety of dance classes for kids aged 2 to 18, focusing on building confidence and discipline.
providers.longDescription: April's Dancing Feet in Brooklyn offers a vibrant space for children to explore various dance styles, including Hip Hop, Gymnastics, Caribbean Dance, Ballet, and Tap. This studio caters to students from toddlers through teens, providing a nurturing environment where kids can learn the fundamentals of each dance form while having fun. Parents can register their children today for an enriching dance experience that fosters creativity, physical fitness, and confidence. Whether it's your little one’s first time stepping into the world of dance or they’re ready to take their skills to the next level, April's Dancing Feet has something for everyone.

providers.name: AquaBeba Halsey
providers.shortDescription: AquaBeba teaches infants, toddlers, and young children the fundamentals of swimming in a safe environment.
providers.longDescription: AquaBeba offers a fully trained instructor-led program for infants through young children, focusing on the fundamentals of swimming in a safe and comfortable environment. The unique curriculum helps babies and parents feel confident and secure in water by teaching breath-holding, independent swimming without flotation devices, and essential safety skills that can be life-saving. Owner Danilo Krvavac, a former Olympic swimmer from Serbia, brings his passion for teaching to every lesson, ensuring each child progresses at their own pace through fun and engaging activities.

providers.name: AquaBeba The Wave
providers.shortDescription: AquaBeba offers swimming lessons for infants, toddlers, and young children, focusing on teaching them the basics in a safe and supportive environment.
providers.longDescription: AquaBeba offers a comprehensive swimming program for children from infants to toddlers, taught by fully trained instructors. The program is tailored to each child's unique abilities and pace, using fun and games to help them relax in the water and develop respect and awareness. It prepares babies for submersion by teaching them to respond to verbal cues and encourages them to swim independently without flotation devices. The program also emphasizes safety skills and independence in and around water. Owner Danilo Krvavac, a former Olympic swimmer and Serbian record holder, opened AquaBeba in Williamsburg, Brooklyn, after the birth of his daughter Penelope.

providers.name: Art's House Schools
providers.shortDescription: Art's House Schools in Coney Island offers dance, music, and fine arts classes for children. These classes focus on providing a strong foundation for performance through skilled instruction.
providers.longDescription: At Art's House Schools, we focus on providing a strong foundation in dance, music, and fine arts through expert instruction. Our goal is to introduce children to the humanities and help them develop self-esteem, confidence, poise, grace, and balance. Since 2005, thousands of students have attended our classes, with many going on to be accepted into specialized junior high and high schools for music, dance, and fine arts.

providers.name: Asphalt Green Battery Park City
providers.address: 212 North End Ave, New York, NY 10282
providers.shortDescription: Asphalt Green's second flagship location in Battery Park City provides swim, sports, and fitness classes, along with a fitness center, training studios, and pools.
providers.longDescription:
Asphalt Green Battery Park City provides a lively and inclusive setting for fitness lovers of all ages and abilities. Located in the center of Battery Park City, it features modern training studios, a comprehensive fitness center, and multiple pools to suit different interests and needs. Weekly classes are offered across various disciplines such as swim lessons, sports training, and fitness programs, making it accessible for both experienced athletes and newcomers.

The facility excels by nurturing a strong community through its programming, which aims to transform lives and foster connections among participants. Memberships grant access to all amenities, ensuring that everyone can participate in activities promoting health, wellness, and personal development. From improving swimming skills to enhancing physical fitness or simply enjoying a fun workout with friends, Asphalt Green Battery Park City welcomes all.

Operating from early morning until late evening on weekdays and weekends, the facility offers flexibility for busy schedules.

providers.name: Asphalt Green Crown Heights
providers.shortDescription: Asphalt Green's Brooklyn location is situated inside the Major R. Owens Health & Wellness Community Center's Carey Gabay Recreation Center in Crown Heights.
providers.longDescription: At Asphalt Green Crown Heights, the experience revolves around community and transformation through fitness and wellness. Weekly classes are available throughout the week for beginners to seasoned athletes. The facility operates from early morning until late evening, offering numerous opportunities for members to engage in activities that enhance physical health and mental well-being. Morning sessions and evening events are always on offer at this lively center. The space uniquely combines a fitness center with educational areas and community organizations, fostering a sense of belonging and shared purpose among its users. Asphalt Green's mission aims to support individuals and build stronger communities through sports, fitness, and play.

providers.name: Asphalt Green Upper East Side
providers.shortDescription: Asphalt Green's Upper East Side center at 555 East 90th Street runs children's swim lessons in two pools, youth sports, an AstroTurf field, after-school programs and a summer day camp.
providers.longDescription: Asphalt Green's original center occupies a block at 555 East 90th Street in Yorkville, built around the barrel-vaulted former asphalt plant the organization is named after. Swimming anchors the children's program: two pools running lessons from water acclimation for babies through stroke development and on to a competitive swim team. Around them are a full-size AstroTurf field, a gym and studios, with youth soccer, basketball, flag football, martial arts and gymnastics-style movement classes, plus after-school programs with school pickup and a summer day camp. It is a non-profit; financial aid is available and it runs free community programming alongside the paid classes.

providers.name: Aviator Sport Club
providers.shortDescription: Aviator Sport Club in Brooklyn offers ice hockey and figure skating programs for kids of all ages. With expert-led classes, children can build confidence and skills on the ice.
providers.longDescription: Aviator Sport Club, situated at Floyd Bennett Field, offers an exceptional environment for youth sports and recreation. Perfect for children interested in ice hockey or figure skating, the club provides structured training programs that cater to both beginners and advanced learners. Expert coaches guide kids through various levels, ensuring they develop skills on and off the ice. Parents can trust Aviator Sport Club to support their child's growth and passion for these winter sports.

providers.name: Aviator Sports and Events Center
providers.shortDescription: The Aviator Sports and Events Center at Floyd Bennett Field offers a variety of activities for children, including gymnastics, ice hockey, skating, soccer, and rock climbing. They also provide weeklong gymnastics camps and a summer day camp for children aged 4 to 15.
providers.longDescription: Aviator Sports and Events Center is located at 3159 Flatbush Avenue, on the Marine Park edge of Brooklyn, in converted hangars at Floyd Bennett Field. It is one of the largest indoor sports complexes in the city, featuring two ice rinks, a full gymnastics gym, indoor turf fields, courts, and a climbing wall. Children's programming is available year-round, offering learn-to-skate and youth hockey, recreational and competitive gymnastics, soccer, and basketball leagues. Gymnastics camps are held weekly for children aged 3 to 16, while the Aviator Sports Summer Day Camp divides ages 4 to 15 into three divisions focusing on sports, arts, and field trips. The complex also accommodates birthday parties and tournaments.

providers.name: Ballet Hispánico
providers.shortDescription: Ballet Hispánico provides dance classes for children and adults in a supportive setting. Their programs are designed for different age groups: Los Pasitos/Little Steps for ages 2-5, Encuentros/Discovery for ages 6-18, La Academia for ages 7-23, and professional programs for older students.
providers.longDescription: Ballet Hispánico focuses on developing dance through a supportive environment that highlights exceptional technique. They offer classes for children from early childhood to professional levels. For young children, there are Los Pasitos/Little Steps classes for ages 2-5. For older children, Encuentros/Discovery classes are available for ages 6-18. La Academia classes cater to students aged 7-23. Older students can participate in professional programs like the Pre & Professional Program, Scholarship Program, Summer & Winter Intensive Programs, and more. Additionally, Ballet Hispánico offers adult classes to help individuals of all ages enhance their movement skills.

providers.name: Bay Ridge Ballet — Children's Dance Classes
providers.shortDescription: Bay Ridge Ballet offers a variety of dance classes from toddler to adult, including ballet, pointe, tap, jazz, hip-hop, modern, tumbling, and boys' classes.
providers.longDescription: Bay Ridge Ballet offers a comprehensive dance education program for children and adults in Brooklyn, NY. From toddlers to seniors, they provide classes in ballet, pointe, tap, jazz, hip-hop, modern, tumbling, and boys' classes. The studio also features pre-professional training programs and private lessons, ensuring personalized instruction. Community outreach includes participation in Nutcracker performances, making it a vibrant part of the local culture. Parents can enroll their children in free trial classes to find the right fit and explore various dance styles. Open house events and auditions for the Nutcracker provide additional opportunities for families to engage with the community.

announcement.title: Current tuition from $415 per semester
announcement.description: Bay Ridge Ballet's 2026/2027 rates page lists $415 tuition per 16-class semester, with multi-class discounts for siblings or multiple classes.

trial.text: FREE TRIAL CLASS

providers.name: Bedstuy Youth Soccer Club
providers.shortDescription: Bedstuy Youth Soccer Club offers soccer classes and camps for boys and girls aged two to ten at Herbert Von King Park during the spring and fall seasons.
providers.longDescription:
Bedstuy Youth Soccer Club offers a structured program divided by season and gender, providing separate classes for boys and girls in both spring and fall. Additionally, they offer matching camp sessions that cater to a wide age range, from two to ten years old. This approach ensures that each age group is served in a manner that is appropriate for their developmental stage, avoiding the challenge of mixing toddlers and elementary-age children in a single group.

The youngest players have their own dedicated track, with a one-hour Saturday class specifically designed to introduce toddlers to the game in a gentle and distinct manner. This class is separate from the afterschool sessions and summer camps that cater to older children in the program. The club operates from Herbert Von King Park, providing a consistent home base in the neighborhood. This stability is beneficial for families looking to establish a regular weekly routine around the soccer classes.

providers.name: Bouldering Project Brooklyn
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn bouldering gym offers youth climbing programs for ages 5-12, including school holiday camps, after-school activities, birthday parties, and youth climbing teams.
providers.longDescription: Climbing is a fun and exciting sport that helps develop resilience, confidence, problem-solving skills, and community building. Bouldering Project’s Youth Programs offer activities tailored to each age group with plenty of climbing challenges, social time, S.T.E.A.M. activities, team-building exercises, yoga, and more during Summer Adventures. After School Programs provide a space for kids to learn basic climbing techniques and terminology while enjoying games both on and off the wall. Birthday parties are also available, offering a day full of climbing and fun with private party spaces. Parents can enjoy a night out with their children through the Parents’ Night Out program.

nextOccurrence.title: Parent's Night Out
nextOccurrence.summary: Held the second-to-last Friday of every month: climbing and activities followed by pizza and a kid-friendly movie.

providers.name: BRAINS Swimming
providers.shortDescription: BRAINS Swimming offers learn-to-swim classes for young children and competitive swim training for older kids. Classes are limited during the school year, with open spots often reserved for those on a wait list.
providers.longDescription: BRAINS Swimming offers structured swimming lessons for young children aged 5 to 7 during the school year, creating an engaging and safe environment where kids can develop essential water skills. These classes are highly sought after, often requiring previous attendance or a place on a waiting list. For older competitive swimmers aged 7 to 12, BRAINS provides tryouts for their Harbor Seals swim team, which involves regular practice sessions from mid-September to mid-June. Parents and children can look forward to structured lessons that foster confidence in the water and build strong swimming abilities. While the team requires consistent attendance and participation in meets, it offers a unique opportunity for young swimmers to excel and compete at a higher level.

providers.name: Breakaway Hoops
providers.address: Dempsey Center, 127 West 127th Street, New York, NY 10027
providers.shortDescription: Breakaway Hoops offers basketball clinics, leagues, and camps for children aged 5 to 15. These programs are led by coaches with over 20 years of combined experience.
providers.longDescription: Breakaway Hoops offers youth basketball programs in Harlem, catering to players from beginner to advanced levels. The Dempsey Center on West 127th Street is the main location for their afterschool clinics. Their programs vary widely, including weekend fundamentals clinics for younger players, a youth developmental league focused on team play, holiday camps, and a summer camp for both boys and girls. Coaches, who have over twenty years of combined experience, are drawn from professional, college, high school, and AAU backgrounds. They work alongside assistant coaches, ensuring a well-rounded and supportive environment for all participants.

providers.name: Bridgeview Soccer Academy
providers.shortDescription: Year-round youth soccer classes are offered in Brooklyn, catering to children from toddler introduction through advanced pre-academy play.
providers.longDescription: Bridgeview Soccer Academy offers year-round soccer classes for children in Brooklyn, providing training both outdoors in good weather and on a covered field during the winter. Classes are organized by age and developmental stage, with Kinder Island for ages 2-5 focusing on balance, coordination, and basic ball touches. For ages 4-7, Fundamentals emphasizes core dribbling, first touch, and passing skills through interactive game sessions. Ages 8-11 benefit from Technique and Game IQ, which enhances finishing, 1v1 play, and decision-making. Advanced Play for ages 12-14 focuses on attacking and defending techniques, preparing students for pre-academy and academy teams. Training occurs in two-week cycles, alternating between technical introduction weeks and weeks of applying skills under game pressure. Licensed coaches also lead a Mommy and Me soccer program for children as young as two, with a parent on the field. Additionally, there is a school-break day program offering soccer practice, tactical lessons, and board games. Bridgeview Soccer Academy also provides classes at daycare centers and schools across Brooklyn, with some schools arranging bus rides to its partner facility at Matchpoint for practice.

trial.text: No charge unless your child enrolls.

providers.name: British Swim School at 904 Pacific
providers.shortDescription: British Swim School's 904 Pacific location in Brooklyn provides year-round swim lessons for children as young as 3 months old and adults. Classes are held in small groups to ensure personalized attention. The school emphasizes a survival-first approach to swimming.
providers.longDescription:
At British Swim School located at 904 Pacific in Brooklyn, swimmers of all ages—from infants to adults and those with special needs—can start their journey to become confident and skilled in the water. The school provides three progressive tiers tailored to different learning stages: Water Acclimation, Water Survival, and Stroke Development. For young families, Tadpole classes offer a fun way for parents to participate alongside their children, helping to build strong bonds while teaching essential safety skills. Older kids and adults can choose from Young Adult, Adult, or Adaptive programs that focus on refining techniques and building endurance.

Each class is carefully structured with a maximum of 4 instructors per Water Safety class and 6 instructors per Tadpole and Stroke Development session, ensuring personalized attention and support. Lessons are held once a week for group lessons, lasting 30 minutes each, while private lessons are available for those needing more focused instruction.

The school prioritizes safety by training its instructors through British Swim School's certification program as well as nationally recognized standards.

providers.name: Broadway TaeKwonDo
providers.shortDescription: Upper West Side Taekwondo offers Tiny/Little Dino classes for children aged 3-6, along with a Junior program for ages 6-12. They also provide Taekwondo and Kickboxing classes for teens and adults.
providers.longDescription: Broadway TaeKwonDo offers martial arts classes for children, teens, and adults located in the Upper West Side. Tiny and Little Dino classes are designed for kids aged 3 to 6, while the Junior program caters to ages 6 to 12. Students then transition to the Teen and Adult program starting at 13 and above. Additionally, the school provides a separate Kickboxing class. New students have the opportunity to try the classes for two weeks, with up to four classes and a complimentary t-shirt, without any commitment.

trial.text: Try up to 4 classes, get a FREE T-shirt, and book your first class right away.

providers.name: Brooklyn Aikikai
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Aikikai offers aikido classes for kids aged 6-14, with sessions on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday.
providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Aikikai is a dedicated aikido school for children aged 6 to 14. Classes are held on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday afternoons, with orientation sessions for new students in September. Parents can enroll their kids twice a year, starting in January and September. The dojo offers a comprehensive program that includes learning etiquette, basic moves, and how to tie the belt during the orientation. Monthly membership fees vary based on a sliding scale, making it accessible to families of different financial backgrounds. Experienced instructors like Kate Savoca, who holds a godan rank, guide students in developing physical strength, flexibility, and important life skills such as focus, perseverance, and respect. Joining Brooklyn Aikikai means embracing a tradition-rich environment where children can grow both physically and mentally.

providers.name: Brooklyn AYSO 473
providers.address: Parade Ground, Caton Avenue & Parkside Avenue, Brooklyn, NY 11218
providers.shortDescription: Volunteer-run AYSO Region 473 offers co-ed and girls recreational soccer for ages 5 to 20, with home games at the Parade Ground south of Prospect Park.
providers.longDescription: Brooklyn AYSO is Region 473 of the American Youth Soccer Organization, a nonprofit, all-volunteer youth soccer league. Its FAQ currently lists eligibility as children born between 1/1/06 and 12/31/20, which spans roughly ages 5 through 20. The league is organized around AYSO Six Philosophies -- Everyone Plays, Balanced Teams, Open Registration, Positive Coaching, Good Sportsmanship and Player Development -- and fields co-ed divisions from a clinic-style entry group through 4v4 and 5v5 formats up to full 9v9 and 11v11 play, alongside separate girls-only divisions at the older age groups. The core Fall season plays on Saturdays, with some Sunday dates, from Sept. through Nov., with games at the Parade Ground south of Prospect Park; a Winter Indoor season moves play to Chelsea Piers Field House on Dean Street, and a Spring season follows the same outdoor-field format as Fall. Every coach, referee and team manager is a parent volunteer, and the region maintains its own game-day safety and incident-reporting rules. A summer camps and clinics program has run in past years, though the league own site notes it is not operating for the current season.

providers.name: Brooklyn Basketball Academy
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Basketball Academy offers a beginner program designed for early coordination and core skill development.
providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Basketball Academy offers a beginner program designed for early coordination and core skill development. The academy evaluates each child individually to place them in the most suitable program based on their current ability.

providers.name: Brooklyn Basketball Training Center
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Basketball's Training Center is located at 140 Flatbush Ave, just across from Barclays Center. They provide after-school and weekend youth training, featuring Shoot 360 technology. Additionally, they offer a first free session for participants.
providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Basketball's Training Center is situated at 140 Flatbush Ave in Downtown Brooklyn, just across from Barclays Center. This facility offers after-school and weekend training programs, featuring 2 full courts, 1 half-court lab, and 9 total hoops. It is the only youth basketball facility in the tri-state area to use Shoot 360 technology, which includes the patented Splash Meter for tracking shooting through high repetition and real-time feedback. Additionally, there is a high-tech passing skill court designed to enhance decision-making, reaction time, speed, and accuracy. A virtual trainer provides guided workouts to improve ball speed, accuracy, and control. New visitors are welcome to book a free initial session.

trial.text: Book First Free Session

providers.name: Brooklyn Botanic Garden Children's Garden
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Botanic Garden's Children's Garden provides hands-on gardening classes for children aged 2 to 13. Participants learn to plant, weed, water, and harvest their own crops and flowers. The classes are led by experienced garden instructors.
providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Botanic Garden's Children's Garden offers a variety of activities for children aged 2 to 13. The program includes planting crops and flowers, art projects, cooking, and nature exploration, all guided by experienced instructors. Classes are organized by age: Trees & Saplings is designed for 2 and 3-year-olds with a caregiver, while Seeds is a drop-off program for 4, 5, and 6-year-olds. City Farmers is available for students in grades 1 through 8. Additionally, a summer Garden Adventures program is available for ages 4 to 13, and Family Gardening Hours are open to children of all ages with an adult. The garden can be accessed at 455 Flatbush Avenue or 990 Washington Avenue.

providers.name: Brooklyn Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Cobble Hill
providers.shortDescription: Cobble Hill martial arts school offers Jiu-Jitsu and karate classes for children, alongside adult classes in Jiu-Jitsu and kickboxing. It is one of several Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu locations in Brooklyn.
providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu's Cobble Hill school offers martial arts classes for men, women, and children in a cooperative, non-competitive setting. The programs focus on building long-term confidence and fitness rather than preparing for tournaments. Kids' Martial Arts classes emphasize self-defense, discipline, and fitness, while Jiu-Jitsu and Kickboxing programs cater to teens and adults. Families interested in trying the program can begin with a private, one-to-one introductory lesson. Cobble Hill is one of several locations for Brooklyn Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu in the borough.

trial.text: Special Introductory Offer! Find out if our program is right for you by signing up for a private, one-to-one introductory lesson.

providers.name: Brooklyn Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Gravesend
providers.shortDescription: Gravesend martial arts school offers Jiu-Jitsu and karate classes for children, alongside adult classes in Jiu-Jitsu and kickboxing. This school is one of several Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu locations in Brooklyn.
providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu's Gravesend school offers martial arts classes for men, women, and children in a cooperative, non-competitive setting. The programs focus on building long-term confidence and fitness rather than preparing for tournaments. Kids' Martial Arts classes emphasize self-defense, discipline, and fitness, while Jiu-Jitsu and Kickboxing programs cater to teens and adults. Families interested in the program can begin with a private, one-to-one introductory lesson. Gravesend is one of several Brooklyn Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu locations in the borough.

trial.text: Special Introductory Offer! Find out if our program is right for you by signing up for a private, one-to-one introductory lesson.

providers.name: Brooklyn Bridge Fencing Club
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Bridge Fencing Club takes kids as young as four from a single introductory lesson through group classes and a full-day summer camp.
providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Bridge Fencing Club describes itself as a welcoming place to start and a serious place to grow, and the program is structured to back that up with an actual path rather than just a slogan. A child's first step is a one-on-one introductory lesson with a coach, no prior experience or equipment needed, which lowers the barrier for a family that has never even seen fencing in person before. From there, kids can continue into a small introductory package that combines private lessons with group classes before deciding whether to join the regular beginner group classes, which run six days a week -- a real, ongoing commitment rather than a once-a-week token class. Summer brings a full-day fencing camp for slightly older kids, described as the only full-day fencing camp in the city, with equipment provided throughout every stage of the program so no family has to buy gear before knowing whether their child even likes the sport.

trial.text: Book Your Child's First Fencing Lesson - $49, one-on-one with an expert coach, 20 minutes, no experience or equipment needed

providers.name: Brooklyn Bridge Park Boathouse
providers.address: Pier 2, Brooklyn Bridge Park, Brooklyn, NY 11201
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Bridge Park Boathouse provides free kayaking sessions for the public and children on certain days, requiring reservations.
providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Bridge Park Boathouse offers free kayaking sessions for the public every Wednesday, Thursday, and Saturday from late May through August, with Saturdays also available in September. Kids aged 7 and older can paddle solo with guardian supervision on summer Sundays, thanks to additional safety boaters from The Kayak Foundation. Appointments open two weeks in advance at 10:00 AM for each session, which start at 10:20 AM, 10:40 AM, and so on. The program is located between Piers 1 and 2 in Brooklyn Bridge Park, with the dock near the roller-skating rink on Pier 2. If you can't secure an appointment, there is a standby form for last-minute opportunities. Kayak polo practice and games are also available to volunteers and their friends or family members.

providers.name: Brooklyn Bridge Park — Nature Storytime
providers.address: 99 Plymouth Street, Brooklyn, NY 11201 (Environmental Education Center)
providers.shortDescription: Once a month, Brooklyn Public Library brings storytime out of the branch and into Brooklyn Bridge Park's Environmental Education Center, pairing a book with the season's nature theme.
providers.longDescription: Nature Storytime takes a familiar library ritual and moves it somewhere a library branch cannot go: the Environmental Education Center inside Brooklyn Bridge Park, on the third Thursday afternoon of every month. Librarians from the Adams Street branch lead the session, with stories, singing and rhymes built around a book chosen to match whatever nature theme the center is focused on that month, so the reading connects directly to the surroundings a child is actually sitting in rather than existing on its own. It is a short, half-hour commitment, easy to fit into an afternoon without derailing the rest of the day, and it happens reliably enough on a set monthly rhythm that it can become a standing date on a family calendar rather than a one-time outing.

providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Center Stage provides a variety of dance classes for children, catering to interests in ballet, hip-hop, and contemporary. Our skilled instructors foster a supportive atmosphere where creativity and confidence thrive. Classes are suitable for both beginners and those with some experience, and they are designed to accommodate different age groups and skill levels. Parents are welcome to join in the fun by observing or participating alongside their children, making it a great family activity that encourages bonding and shared interests.

providers.name: Brooklyn Children's Museum

providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Children's Museum, established since 1899, offers a unique blend of cultural experiences through interactive exhibits like the Empire Skate of Mind, AirMaze, and Totally Tots. Perfect for children from babies to big kids, it’s an ideal venue for birthday celebrations and school trips that promote learning and fun. Parents can enjoy knowing their children are engaged in educational activities while exploring these vibrant spaces.

announcement.title: Serving families since 1899

providers.name: Brooklyn Crescents Lacrosse
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Crescents has run youth lacrosse across Brooklyn, Manhattan and Queens for over 20 years, from first-timers age three through high school travel teams.
providers.longDescription: Twenty years is a long run for a youth sports program in a city where leagues start and fold within a season, and Brooklyn Crescents wears that history as a real credential rather than a footnote. The program's range runs from the very first introduction to the sport at age three all the way up to travel competitive teams for high schoolers, which means a family doesn't have to switch programs as a kid grows more serious about the sport -- Crescents can be the only lacrosse program a child ever needs. Fall lacrosse returns across Brooklyn, Manhattan and Queens each year, open to every skill level rather than sorting kids into a beginner-only track and a competitive-only track with nothing in between. That two-decade continuity also means the coaching staff has had a long time to refine how it teaches the sport to a three-year-old differently than it teaches a varsity-bound teenager.

providers.address: Prospect Park, 9th Street Entrance, Brooklyn, NY 11215
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Kids Run provides weekday and Saturday running classes for children aged 6 to 15 at the 9th Street entrance to Prospect Park, guided by a USATF-registered coach. The program caters to both beginners and advanced runners with various tracks.
providers.longDescription:
Brooklyn Kids Run is a USATF-registered program tailored for children aged 6 to 15 who aspire to enhance their running abilities. The 10-week Fall session offers diverse classes that focus on building strength, speed, and endurance through a combination of running and stretching exercises. Classes take place in the scenic setting of Prospect Park, where participants can enjoy both road and trail running.

The program is structured with specific age groups and experience levels to ensure each child receives personalized attention. Monday, Wednesday, and Friday sessions are designed for experienced runners aged 7 to 13 who can comfortably run a mile. These classes provide an engaging environment that challenges and supports young athletes as they develop their skills.

Tuesday's Speed Training class is reserved for experienced runners aged 10 to 14 who have successfully completed a 5k distance and passed the tryout. This session offers advanced training to help these runners push their limits and improve their performance.

For beginners or intermediate runners aged 11 to 15, Monday classes offer a more relaxed pace that allows them to build confidence and foundational skills in running. These sessions run from 5:20 to 6:40 PM.

Saturdays feature two distinct classes for different age groups. Novice runners aged 6 to 12 can join the beginner class from 12:10 to 1:30 PM, while experienced runners aged 10 to 14 who can run 1 to 3 miles participate in the intermediate session from 10:30 to 12:00 PM. All classes are conveniently located at the 9th street entrance of Prospect Park near the Lafayette monument in Park Slope, Brooklyn.

providers.name: Brooklyn Lacrosse Club
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Lacrosse Club is a 100% volunteer-run nonprofit bringing youth lacrosse to Brooklyn kids, coed through 4th grade and split by gender through 6th-12th.
providers.longDescription: Brooklyn Lacrosse Club was built specifically around access: its own stated mission is removing the cost, perception and logistical barriers that keep lacrosse -- still an unfamiliar sport in much of urban Brooklyn -- out of reach for kids who'd otherwise never get a stick in their hands. The club is entirely volunteer-run, with no paid staff drawing a salary from what families pay to play, and passed its tenth anniversary in 2022. Play is coed through 4th grade, then splits by gender: boys continue together through 12th grade, girls through 6th grade. The club's growth and coaching approach have drawn outside attention, including a feature in the NYC Short Documentary Film Festival built around cofounder and executive director Khalid West. Its main season runs in the fall, with registration opening well ahead of the first practice each year.

providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn's squash academy is the only one dedicated to this sport, featuring six courts. It offers 5-week junior and tournament programs for children aged 6 to 18. These programs are taught by former world-ranked professionals and D1 champions.
providers.longDescription:
Brooklyn Squash Academy (BSA) offers a variety of squash programs in Brooklyn, with a focus on providing a world-class experience. They have 6 courts and over 30 weekly sessions, led by coaches who are former world-ranked professionals and D1 champions. 

The Junior Intro Program is a 5-week session lasting 45 minutes per session, designed for ages 6-12. This program is ideal for beginners, covering essential grip and swing basics, court movement games, and rally building. 

For ages 6-17, the Junior Programs offer another 5-week session, also lasting 45 minutes per session. This program progresses from advanced-beginner to intermediate clinics, focusing on stroke development and small group classes. 

The Tournament Squad Program is a 5-week session lasting 1.5 hours per session, aimed at ages 10-18. This program combines match play, strategy sessions, fitness and conditioning, and mental toughness training, preparing players for ranked tournaments. 

BSA also provides Adult Squash Programs, including clinics, leagues, and cardio squash sessions. They have hosted over 10 events and tournaments, and their coaching staff is led by Program Director Omer Khalifa and Assistant Program Director Mohamed Ayman.

providers.longDescription:

The program begins with pre-season workouts in January and February, followed by outdoor practices from March to the summer games and scrimmages. In August, a sleepaway camp is offered to further enhance skills before the fall season starts in November.

Parents can register their children for upcoming sessions and choose to pay in installments. For detailed information on fees and schedules, visit the official website.

Our beginner classes are designed for kids aged 6-12, providing a safe and enjoyable environment to learn essential climbing skills. Parents can watch their children develop footwork, grip techniques, balance, body positioning, and safety protocols, such as proper harness use and belaying basics. Enroll your little climbers today and watch them reach new heights!

providers.name: Chernomorets USA
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Soccer Academy offers soccer practices for children aged 4 to 14, along with additional sports programs during all school breaks.
providers.longDescription: Chernomorets USA, or the Black Sea - Chernomorets Soccer Academy, is located in Brooklyn and offers soccer programs for children aged 4 to 14. In addition to regular practices, the academy provides sports programs during all school breaks, specifically for the same age group. Parents can anticipate their children participating in skill development, teamwork, and physical fitness through structured sessions. Children will have the chance to improve their soccer skills while enjoying enjoyable activities during holidays.

providers.name: Children's Museum of Manhattan
providers.shortDescription: The Children's Museum of Manhattan runs a research-backed early childhood curriculum on the Upper West Side, from Friday music sessions for babies through gentle-separation preschool prep.
providers.longDescription: The Children's Museum of Manhattan treats its Early Childhood Classes as an extension of a research-backed curriculum, not a side activity bolted onto museum hours, with expert educators running each session rather than museum staff filling in. Little Birds is built for the museum's youngest learners, using music and movement specifically to strengthen the bond between a child and their caregiver while building early social and cognitive skills. Preschool Prep takes the opposite approach for slightly older toddlers: a gentle-separation class that eases a child away from a caregiver gradually, through play, art and storytelling, rather than a hard drop-off on day one. Both classes run in fall terms tied to the school calendar rather than as drop-in sessions, and popular sections have sold out before the term even starts.

providers.name: Children's Tumbling
providers.shortDescription: Tribeca Gymnastics Studio provides creative, non-competitive tumbling classes for children from toddler age through pre-teen years.
providers.longDescription:
Children's Tumbling is located in Tribeca, Lower Manhattan, and has been teaching gymnastics since 1978. Their classes are designed to be inclusive and engaging for children from toddlers to pre-teens. Unlike competitive teams, they focus on tumbling and movement skills through imaginative stories, lively music, and colorful costumes. With small class sizes, each child gets personalized attention in a supportive environment.

For toddlers, the curriculum includes fun activities like climbing mats, swinging on trapeze and rings, jumping on trampolines, and navigating rope ladders to develop gross motor skills. Older children build upon these basics with advanced floor exercises and apparatus work using rhythmic ribbons, hoops, tightropes, circus webs, aerial silks, and stilts.

The studio also provides private and semi-private lessons for families who want more focused coaching in specific skill sets. These sessions are tailored to help each child progress at their own pace.

providers.name: ChoElite New York City
providers.shortDescription: This Taekwondo school on East 105th Street offers classes in both Kukkiwon and World Taekwondo Federation styles for children and adults.
providers.longDescription: ChoElite New York City is a Taekwondo school that teaches the Kukkiwon and World Taekwondo Federation styles, recognized by the International Olympic Committee. The school's curriculum is designed for international Black Belt certification, with all instructors being Kukkiwon-certified Black Belts. Programs are organized by age: Elite Tigers is for 4 and 5-year-olds, using games and exercises to develop motor skills. Traditional Taekwondo, starting at age 6, covers white belt through black belt, focusing on self-defense, confidence, respect, and focus. Advanced students join the Elite Competition Team, which competes at the highest levels. Master Slavcho Rachev, a 7th Degree Black Belt and Bulgaria Olympic Taekwondo National Team coach, is the head instructor. Instructor Maria Marcheva, a 4th Degree Black Belt and national coach, and Instructor Asenia Pulina, a 3rd Degree Black Belt and Poomsae National Champion, also contribute to the school. ChoElite offers private lessons in taekwondo, kickboxing, and fitness, which can be conducted at a student's home, building, gym, or local park, alongside an Adult Class.

providers.name: Church Street Boxing Gym Chelsea
providers.shortDescription: Church Street Boxing Gym provides classes in boxing, Muay Thai, Brazilian Jiu Jitsu, and kids' programs designed to build confidence and self-defense skills.
providers.longDescription: Church Street Boxing Gym offers a range of workouts designed to help you achieve your fitness goals. Our experienced coaches will teach you proper boxing form, technique, and execution. Muay Thai provides a comprehensive full-body workout that improves cardiovascular endurance and flexibility. Brazilian Jiu Jitsu focuses on grappling and ground fighting techniques, ideal for self-defense. Kids and teens can develop confidence and discipline in a safe and supportive environment.

providers.longDescription: Church Street Boxing Gym offers a comprehensive range of martial arts classes in Downtown New York. Their Boxing program, led by experienced coaches who have competed worldwide, emphasizes proper form, technique, and execution, alongside conditioning and strength drills. Muay Thai provides a full-body workout that enhances cardiovascular endurance, builds strength, and improves flexibility. Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu focuses on grappling and ground fighting techniques, using technique to subdue and control an opponent, making it an effective self-defense system. The Kids & Teens program fosters confidence, discipline, and self-defense skills in a safe and enjoyable setting. Teen Boxing encourages teens to appreciate exercise. New members can participate in a free trial with a team member before starting personalized training with a coach.

providers.name: City Parks Foundation
providers.shortDescription: CityParks Play provides a range of sports activities for children aged 6 to 17 in New York City parks, including tennis, golf, soccer, and track & field.
providers.longDescription: City Parks Foundation provides a variety of free sports programs for children and seniors across New York City's parks. The foundation focuses on teaching kids ages 6-17 and seniors over 60 how to play tennis, golf, soccer, and track & field. Programs include beginner lessons, tournaments, leagues, and special events with professional instructors. For more information or to get involved, visit their website.

providers.name: Columbus Gym
providers.shortDescription: Columbus Gym offers gymnastics classes for children aged 10 months to 12 years, focusing on physical, social, and emotional growth. The program includes adult-participation sessions and independent gym classes with a variety of equipment.
providers.longDescription: Columbus Gym in New York has been fostering self-esteem and physical activity through gymnastics since 1988. For children aged 10 months to 12 years, they offer Tiny Tot Fitness, a program for younger kids with adult participation, exploring equipment like beams, bars, rings, and trampoline. As kids grow, Mini Gym provides independent exploration in 40-minute sessions, enhancing skills through routines such as rolls, handstands, and advanced moves on various apparatuses. Parents can join the adult-participation program to explore gymnastics alongside their children. The studio features a 2,500 sq ft space with sports stations, songs, parachute fun, bubbles, and stamps for added enjoyment. Gymnastics at Columbus Gym boosts core strength, flexibility, agility, balance, and confidence, setting kids up for success in various sports or active living.

providers.name: Combat Club
providers.shortDescription: Tribeca offers a self-defense and martial arts academy for children aged 5 to 14. This comprehensive program combines Krav Maga, Muay Thai, boxing, and Jiu Jitsu to develop essential life skills.
providers.longDescription: Combat Club's Tribeca self-defense academy, established in 2010, offers a comprehensive hybrid program blending Krav Maga, Muay Thai, boxing, and Jiu Jitsu grappling. Instructors are highly skilled black belt KMI instructors, and the program emphasizes life skills alongside fighting techniques. These skills include self-confidence, leadership, focus, self-discipline, and practical self-defense. The academy caters to children aged 5 to 14, regardless of prior experience. New students are encouraged to participate in a two-week trial, which includes a complimentary uniform, before committing to a monthly membership. Regular training, at least twice a week, is recommended to build momentum.

providers.name: Coney Island Training the Youth of New York
providers.shortDescription: Coney Island Training the Youth (CITY) offers football classes for kids aged 5-12. Focus on fast play and developing a champion mindset.
providers.longDescription: Coney Island Training the Youth of New York offers a comprehensive program designed to support young athletes in their development and preparation for college. This inclusive environment caters to both boys and girls, providing competitive football seasons through in-house and travel teams. Parents can expect their children to engage in a safe and fun atmosphere that nurtures athletic skills while also fostering personal growth. Children will have the opportunity to participate in rigorous training sessions, learn teamwork, and develop essential life skills. Together, parents and kids can explore the program's offerings, meet coaches, and sign up for teams that best fit their interests and abilities.

providers.name: Court 16 Downtown Brooklyn
providers.address: 445 Albee Square W Suite 4-500, Brooklyn, NY 11201
providers.shortDescription: Court 16's Downtown Brooklyn club is a 28,000 sq. ft. indoor facility that includes tennis and pickleball courts. It also features a Kids Tennis Academy that provides private, semi-private, and group lessons for children. There are five court sizes available, and a kids trial is offered.
providers.longDescription: Court 16's flagship club located in Downtown Brooklyn spans 28,000 square feet and serves as the primary venue for its Tennis Academy, aimed at young athletes and adults. This facility is unique in offering five different court sizes, including a full-size court, making it ideal for various skill levels. It also houses the new Brooklyn Tennis Academy. The club features 44 FT and 60 FT USTA-sanctioned courts, along with a 78 FT full tennis court and pickleball courts, which are the only permanent indoor pickleball courts in Downtown Brooklyn. For children, the Kids Tennis Academy takes a comprehensive approach, placing kids into appropriate groups based on their age and progress. Classes are available in private, semi-private, and group formats, maintaining a student-to-instructor ratio of 5:1 on the 36' court and 6:1 on the 60' court. The academy operates during fall and spring seasons for about 20 weeks each, with an additional summer season open to non-members. To participate in Academy classes outside the summer, a Court 16 Membership is required. Families can book a Kids Trial session before committing to enrollment.

providers.name: Creativity Soccer Pro
providers.shortDescription: Brooklyn Leading Soccer Program provides year-round, age-specific soccer classes for children aged 2 to 12. They also offer a Goal Girls program, a DOE-approved after-school cohort, and camps held at parks and partner schools across Brooklyn.
providers.longDescription: Creativity Soccer Pro offers weekly soccer classes for children aged 2 to 12, divided into three stages: Mini Meg (ages 2-5, 40-45 minutes, 10 weeks, focus on fun), Raw Dribblers (ages 6-8, 50-60 minutes, 10 weeks, focus on technical development), and Internal League (ages 9-12, 60 minutes, 10 weeks). Classes are held weekly during the Fall, Winter, Spring, and Summer seasons, with options for both weekend and weekday attendance. The Talent Development Center is designed for players aged 4 to 8, featuring weekly practices and monthly small-sided games against local clubs. Sessions last 75 minutes, and advanced players have the opportunity to join the travel team and compete in leagues such as the Cosmopolitan Junior Soccer League, New York Club Soccer League, and State Cup games. A Goal Girls program is available for girls, and the Creative After School Cohort is an DOE-approved program for students in grades K through 6, meeting at various partner schools. Saturday Fun Day offers a three-hour program every Saturday, combining soccer, obstacle courses, chess, and homework assistance for children aged 3 to 10. Facilities include parks, indoor turf, gymnasiums, schools, and outdoor fields, with coaches certified in USFF, NSCAA, NASPE, and UEFA.

providers.name: Crossbar Toddler Open Play
providers.shortDescription: Crossbar turns its Upper West Side soccer space into a toddler open-play spot every weekday morning, with soccer balls and toys in a climate-controlled indoor setting.
providers.longDescription: Crossbar opens its Upper West Side venue to toddlers every weekday morning for open, unstructured play with soccer balls and other toys, in a space that stays climate-controlled year-round. There is nothing to sign a child up for and nothing to practice toward: it is simply a safe indoor place to run around, kick a ball, and burn off energy on a school-day morning, whatever the weather is doing outside. The venue includes a café on site, so a parent can grab a coffee and something to eat while keeping an eye on their toddler. It is the kind of low-pressure morning outing that fits easily into a week without needing to be planned days in advance.

The school also runs an After School Program and a Summer Camp, plus adult BJJ and MMA classes. The training space is a 2,000 square-foot main floor with 12 foot ceilings, new mats, a climate-controlled waiting area, open seating for parents to watch, and complimentary Wi-Fi. New students can try a free class before committing to a program.

providers.name: DeadWeight Martial Arts
providers.shortDescription: DeadWeight Martial Arts in Brooklyn offers Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Muay Thai, and MMA conditioning. They also provide a weekly kids' class called Tap & Tumble.
providers.longDescription: DeadWeight Martial Arts is a Brooklyn gym nestled on Marcus Garvey Blvd, dedicated to offering Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Muay Thai, and MMA conditioning classes. Their Tap & Tumble Kids BJJ program caters to young learners from Monday through Thursday in the early evening hours, focusing on foundational techniques such as positional control, takedowns, balance drills, escapes, safe falling and rolling, and mat awareness. The class environment is designed to foster respect, teamwork, and emotional regulation while blending technical instruction with engaging partner drills and age-appropriate games, making it accessible for both beginners and experienced kids alike. For adults, Deadweight BJJ (Gi) grappling, Muay-Thai striking, and an MMA Conditioning Class provide a robust training experience that caters to various skill levels and interests.

providers.longDescription: Diamondheart's Bushwick space is built specifically around grappling and striking as separate disciplines rather than one general martial arts curriculum: a full second floor of dedicated mat space for Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, both gi and no-gi, running seven days a week across morning and afternoon sessions, alongside Muay Thai and Boxing programs on the gym's other floor. The pitch is explicitly low-commitment -- a free trial runs seven days with no obligation attached, long enough for a student to actually try more than one class before deciding whether self-defense, competition or general fitness is the reason they're really there.

providers.name: Dodge YMCA — Traditional Summer Camp (2026)
providers.shortDescription: Dodge YMCA runs four distinct summer camp tracks -- Traditional, Kinder, Swim and Big Messy Art -- for ages 4 to 12, with registration for the next season opening each December.
providers.longDescription: Dodge YMCA's Traditional Summer Camp for kids aged 5-10 is an inclusive and enriching experience where children grow bolder, braver, and brighter. Located at 225 Atlantic Avenue in Brooklyn, NY, this camp offers a unique blend of traditional activities like arts and crafts, science experiments, and theme days, alongside essential skills such as swimming. Camp runs from June 29 to August 21, with four two-week sessions that include extended hours for added convenience. Parents can register their children starting December 2026, ensuring they secure a spot in this transformative summer adventure. The camp fosters social and emotional growth through structured activities and team building exercises, all while upholding the YMCA’s core values of respect, caring, honesty, and responsibility.

providers.name: Dribbl
providers.shortDescription: Dribbl offers a fun, recreational basketball program for kids aged 3-14 in New York City. The program focuses on teaching fundamental skills and is known for its experienced staff and high coach-to-player ratio.
providers.longDescription: For over 25 years, Dribbl has been the go-to instructional basketball program for young athletes in New York City and the Hamptons. Known for its positive and supportive environment, Dribbl enrolls more than 1,000 families annually. The program is praised for its experienced staff and high coach-to-player ratio, ensuring that each child receives personalized attention. Parents can register their kids for summer camps, fall sessions, winter programs, girls' leagues, boys' leagues, and travel teams. Dribbl has been recognized as the Best Basketball Clinic in New York magazine’s annual “Best of New York” issue.

providers.name: Dance Theatre of Harlem School — Saturday Youth Drop-In Classes
providers.shortDescription: Dance Theatre of Harlem offers Saturday Youth Drop-In Classes for students to explore dance.
providers.longDescription: Dance Theatre of Harlem offers a Saturday drop-in program for young people in the neighborhood, with no auditions or prior training needed. This low-commitment format allows families to attend a single class without committing to the full-year program. Beginners are encouraged to join the ballet class, which focuses on fundamentals like placement and rotation in a supportive and uplifting environment. Teens have the option to participate in two additional tracks that emphasize rhythm and culture, taught by the school's faculty. For families already familiar with Dance Theatre of Harlem's professional stage reputation, this Saturday program provides an accessible entry point into the same building.

providers.name: Dynamics Rhythmic Gymnastics
providers.shortDescription: Dynamics Rhythmic Gymnastics at the Shorefront Y is a USA Gymnastics-registered club that provides rhythmic gymnastics training for children aged 3 and up.
providers.longDescription: Dynamics Rhythmic Gymnastics, based at the Shorefront YM-YWHA, is an officially registered USA Gymnastics club that has been preparing young athletes for state, regional and national competitions since 2005. The program is designed to give each student individualized attention, whether a child is new to rhythmic gymnastics or already has prior experience. Classes begin with beginner-level training, where young gymnasts take their first steps in the sport, and progress through a competitive program that ranges from Level 3 to Elite. Dynamics Rhythmic Gymnastics welcomes children ages 3 and up. The coaching team includes Irina Aksenova, a USAG Professional Member and Safe Sport Certified former Ukrainian National Team member with over 10 years of experience as a Head Coach and Program Director, and Galina Drozdova, who began her rhythmic gymnastics journey in Saint Petersburg, Russia and competed for Dynamics RG at the Elite level.

providers.name: Dynamites Youth Soccer
providers.shortDescription: Dynamites Youth Soccer offers soccer classes for boys and girls aged 4 to 14. Try-outs are open, with a free first lesson available.
providers.longDescription: Dynamites Youth Soccer provides soccer training for children in Brooklyn, focusing on individual attention and skill development. The program caters to both beginners and advanced players, offering recreational and competitive league options as well as private lessons. With over 15 years of coaching experience, Coach Arturo ensures a safe, fun, friendly, and inclusive environment. Try-outs are open for ages 4 to 14, with the first lesson being free. Parents can contact the club by phone or text to schedule a try-out.

providers.longDescription: Located in Brooklyn, the Elite Wrestling Academy provides a range of wrestling programs for young athletes. They specialize in teaching Folkstyle, Freestyle, and Greco-Roman techniques. Sessions are scheduled on Monday, Wednesday, Friday evenings, and Sunday afternoons, catering to both high school students and adults. The academy is open to beginners as well as those with prior experience and operates under the guidance of a dedicated team of coaches, trainers, and support staff focused on delivering top-quality wrestling education and training.

providers.name: Extreme Kids & Crew
providers.shortDescription: Extreme Kids & Crew provides a range of classes for neurodivergent youth, focusing on coding, dance, gaming, and music. These programs aim to develop social-emotional skills within a supportive community.
providers.longDescription: Extreme Kids & Crew focuses on fostering an inclusive environment for neurodivergent young people by providing engaging programs that highlight individual strengths. They offer classes in coding, dance, gaming, and music, all designed to develop social-emotional skills in a supportive and safe space. Additionally, their family programs welcome siblings, parents, and other family members to participate in a judgment-free setting.

providers.name: Fastbreak Sports
providers.shortDescription: A youth sports facility on the Upper East Side offering basketball, flag football, cheer and dance, and multi-sport classes, camps, and teams for kids from toddler age through high school.
providers.longDescription: Fastbreak Sports runs youth sports programs out of its own Upper East Side facility, working with athletes from a toddler's first movement class through a high schooler's more competitive training. Families can filter programs by age, neighborhood, sport, season, and type to find classes, camps, or teams that fit, choosing from basketball, flag football, cheer and dance, and multi-sport options across the Upper East Side, Upper West Side, and Downtown. Beyond regular classes, Fastbreak hosts birthday parties that mix sports and non-sport activities like arts and crafts and inflatables, and offers one-on-one and small-group private coaching built around an individual athlete's goals. The program also runs travel teams, including tryouts for its Metro United, BSNY, and FB Elite AAU squads, plus a travel flag football program for kids ages 8 to 14.

providers.shortDescription: FC Harlem is a Harlem-based youth soccer club pairing the sport with the neighborhood's own culture and creative identity.
providers.longDescription: FC Harlem's own public presence leans more on brand identity than program detail -- its site describes itself as a football club "driven by curiosity and built on purpose," rooted specifically in Harlem rather than a generic citywide operation. What is clear is the core offering: youth soccer, run from and for the neighborhood, with the club's identity deliberately tied to Harlem's own culture, music and design sensibility rather than treating the sport as interchangeable with any other city program. A family drawn to a club that presents itself this way is choosing a specific neighborhood identity alongside the coaching itself.

providers.name: Five Points Lacrosse
providers.shortDescription: Five Points Lacrosse offers a girls' lacrosse program for children aged 12U to varsity-level Daybreak and Skills Sessions for grades 3-12. These sessions are held at Bishop Loughlin in Fort Greene and Stephen Gaynor School in Manhattan.
providers.longDescription: Five Points Lacrosse is a dedicated resource for the NYC girls lacrosse community, established by its founders after observing many top youth players leave the boroughs for club teams far away to pursue advanced play. This organization provides advanced training led by accredited coaches and a well-established curriculum. The program includes teams such as the 12U Hudson Dusters, which focus on core skills, athleticism, and lacrosse IQ; the 14U Bowery, where players specialize in positions and deepen their stick skills, dodging, and team defensive slide packages; the 40 Thieves, designed for players aiming for varsity; and Daybreak, the varsity training program. Team practices occur on Sundays and weeknights at Bishop Loughlin in Brooklyn, with skills sessions held on Fridays at the Stephen Gaynor School in Manhattan. Skills sessions are also available separately by grade: Grades 3-4 in Brooklyn on Sundays from 9-10 a.m. at Bishop Loughlin, Fort Greene; Grades 3-4 in Manhattan on Fridays from 6-7 p.m.; Grades 5-8 in Manhattan on Fridays from 7-8 p.m.; and Grades 9-12 in Manhattan on Fridays from 8-9 p.m., all at the Stephen Gaynor School. Additionally, the teams participate in out-of-state tournaments like the Knickerbocker Classic, Victory Fall Classic, and Platinum Games. The organization's tagline is "Built in the boroughs. Coached to compete."

Weekend birthday parties are also part of the offering, and parents are asked to call ahead to set up a date. Beyond scheduled classes and parties, Focus takes part in the wider community through self-defense classes and visits to local schools, and keeps current families updated on schedule changes and events through its own Instagram account. Anyone with questions about classes, parties, or community programs can reach the gym directly by phone or email.

providers.longDescription: Free Kickers NYC is dedicated to nurturing young soccer players by enhancing their skills, boosting confidence, fostering teamwork, and instilling a lasting love for the sport. Kids can join competitive teams and develop essential skills like discipline, teamwork, and a healthy lifestyle. providers.name: Gleason's Gym
providers.shortDescription: Gleason's Gym, a Brooklyn boxing institution established in 1937, has a rich history of training legendary fighters like Jake LaMotta, Muhammad Ali, and Roberto Duran. The gym offers Pee Wee Boxing classes led by Coach Liza for children aged 4 to 9 and 10 to 16.
providers.longDescription: Gleason's Gym has been a Brooklyn boxing treasure since 1937 and is one of the last of New York City's thriving boxing gyms -- the training headquarters for legends including Jake LaMotta, Muhammad Ali and Roberto Duran, with 136 World Champions having trained inside its walls. Its Pee Wee Boxing classes, taught by Coach Liza, teach the Basics of Boxing through drills, mitt work and calisthenics, covering self-defense moves and building physical fitness, discipline, self-confidence and concentration. Pee Wee is for 4-9 yrs old and Kids is for 10-16 yrs old. Private 1-1 sessions are by appointment Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday; a limited-enrollment group class (drills, sparring) meets Thursday 5:30pm - 6:30pm and Saturday 11:30am - 12:30pm, both requiring advance reservation. Gleason's Daily Membership rate is additional to class fees. The gym is open Mon-Fri 5AM-10:00PM and Sat & Sun 6AM-6:00PM.

nextOccurrence.summary: Limited-enrollment group class (drills, sparring), advance reservation required. Private 1-on-1 sessions also available by appointment Mon/Tue/Thu/Sat.

providers.name: Glory Martial Arts Center
providers.shortDescription: Glory Martial Arts Center provides Kids Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu and Kids Muay Thai Kickboxing classes. These classes are part of a martial arts school located in Brooklyn and Staten Island. The school welcomes new students to try a class without any risk.
providers.longDescription: Glory Martial Arts Center is recognized as Brooklyn and Staten Island's top martial arts school, where children develop leadership skills through discipline and focus. The center also offers fitness and safety programs for adults, with classes designed to be both fun and effective. In Brooklyn, kids can participate in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu and Muay Thai Kickboxing, while adults have options for Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu, Mixed Martial Arts, Muay Thai Kickboxing, Women's Only Martial Arts, and Strength and Conditioning. New students are encouraged to try a class without any commitment, and many members report seeing noticeable improvements within just one week.
